requirement:
Applying a source edit MUST preserve the input fingerprints of every recorded
assessment. A completed reassessment records its own observed inputs under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.delivered_inputs`.
rationale:
I found no test-adequacy gap for `requirements.authoring.persistence.fingerprints`. I did not read the implementation.

Obligations derived from the requirement:
1. Applying a source edit MUST preserve the input fingerprints of every recorded assessment.
2. A completed reassessment records its own observed inputs under `requirements.authoring.delivered_inputs`. That requirement is cited as context, so I did not reassess its own tests.

How the tests cover them:
- `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[an_applied_reference_keeps_the_original_read_and_reassessment_records_the_edit]` runs a failed assessment with an `add_reference` correction that edits `src/lib.rs`. A reassessment follows and succeeds.
  - The test captures the evidence record at turn 4, which is after the edit was applied and before the reassessment finished. It asserts that this record has `determination` false.
  - It asserts that the record's `inputs` still contain the pre-edit `outline_input` of `src/lib.rs`. That input is a whole-file read, so any refresh after the edit would change it.
  - It asserts that the record's `references` equal the pre-edit reference-set digest. It also asserts that this digest differs from the post-edit digest, so the edit really changed the references.
  - For the final success record, it asserts that `inputs` contain the post-edit `outline_input` and that `references` equal the post-edit digest. This covers the reassessment recording its own observed inputs.
- `fn[stale_and_already_present_references_do_not_retry_unchanged_inputs]` covers the cases where no edit is applied: a stale item and a reference that is already present.
  - It asserts that the file stays unchanged, or is the externally changed version in the stale case.
  - It asserts that the recorded `inputs` still contain the originally observed fingerprint. In the stale case it also asserts that this fingerprint differs from the current one. So the record keeps the fingerprint from the original read, not a refreshed one.

The tests assert only the pre-edit whole-file input, not every input. That is enough here. The edit only changes `src/lib.rs`, so a refresh of its fingerprints would show up in the inputs and the reference digest that the tests do check.

mandatory inputs, additional reads, and selected search dependencies under
{cite}`requirements.definitions.inputs`. The harness MUST create these records

itself so ordinary evidence validation can check them later.
